title: Euler's Formula Balanced Equation Visualization
full_prompt: Write a Manim script that visualizes Euler's formula (V - E + F = 2) using a dynamic graph representation. The scene should start by displaying the equation 'V - E + F = 2' at the top of the screen. Underneath each variable (V, E, F), display its corresponding integer value, initialized to 1, 0, and 1 respectively for a trivial graph (one vertex, zero edges, and one outer face). Create a graph structure with vertices (dots), edges (lines), and colored faces (polygons). Start the visualization by showing a single vertex labeled as a 'Trivial graph' with an arrow pointing to it. Flash the variables V, F, and E in the equation sequentially, fading in their initial values (1, 0, 1) and briefly highlighting the background to represent the outer face. Then, animate the addition of a new edge and a new vertex, showing how the counts of V and E increment dynamically while maintaining the balance of the equation.

visual_techniques: Graph rendering with vertices, edges, and faces
Custom rate functions (there_and_back) for background flashing

common_failure_modes.pattern: Using ManimGL-specific InteractiveScene in ManimCE without fallback
common_failure_modes.note: InteractiveScene is exclusive to ManimGL. For ManimCE, use Scene.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Using TexText instead of Tex or Tex with text blocks in ManimCE
common_failure_modes.note: TexText is a ManimGL class; ManimCE uses Tex with standard LaTeX text commands.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Incorrect indexing of Tex characters for V, E, F variables
common_failure_modes.note: Hardcoded character indexing like equation[char][0] can break if the LaTeX compiler groups characters differently.
